mcus.name: Apollo3 Blue
mcus.description: Ultra-low-power 48 MHz (96 MHz burst) Cortex-M4F with BLE 5.0, 1 MB flash and 384 KB SRAM at about 6 uA/MHz, suited to coin-cell wearables, voice and TinyML. Use the SparkFun Artemis module to avoid the BGA.

mcus.name: AT32F403A
mcus.description: 240 MHz Cortex-M4F with up to 1 MB flash and 224 KB SRAM, crystal-less USB FS, 2x CAN, 2x SDIO and 8 UARTs; a fast, cheap STM32F103/F303 upgrade.

mcus.name: AT32F415
mcus.description: Cheap 150 MHz Cortex-M4 with USB FS OTG (host/device) and DFU bootloader, CAN, SDIO and 5 UARTs from about $1.

mcus.name: AT32F421
mcus.description: Value 120 MHz Cortex-M4 with up to 64 KB flash, 2 USART/I2C/SPI and a comparator for under $0.90; a fast STM32F030/G030 alternative.

mcus.name: ESP32
mcus.description: The classic dual-core 240 MHz Wi-Fi + Bluetooth Classic/BLE SoC; huge community, Ethernet MAC, CAN, SD host and cheap pre-certified WROOM modules.

mcus.name: ESP32-S2
mcus.description: Single-core 240 MHz Wi-Fi SoC with native USB OTG, lots of GPIO and touch pins; good for USB gadgets that need Wi-Fi but not Bluetooth.

mcus.name: ESP32-S3
mcus.description: Dual-core 240 MHz Wi-Fi + BLE 5 SoC with native USB, camera/LCD interfaces, vector instructions for AI and up to 16 MB octal PSRAM; the go-to ESP32 for new designs.

mcus.name: ESP32-C2 (ESP8684)
mcus.description: Cheapest Espressif Wi-Fi + BLE 5 chip: 120 MHz RISC-V with in-package flash in a tiny 4x4 mm QFN; an ESP8266 replacement for simple connected devices.

mcus.name: ESP32-C3
mcus.description: Low-cost 160 MHz RISC-V Wi-Fi + BLE 5 SoC with built-in USB serial/JTAG; the cheap, easy default for small connected sensors and controllers.

mcus.name: ESP32-C5
mcus.description: 240 MHz RISC-V SoC with dual-band (2.4 + 5 GHz) Wi-Fi 6, BLE, Thread/Zigbee and two CAN-FD controllers; pick it when 2.4 GHz is congested or you need 5 GHz.
mcus.core: RISC-V 32-bit (RV32IMAC) HP core + 48 MHz LP RISC-V core

mcus.name: ESP32-C6
mcus.description: 160 MHz RISC-V SoC with Wi-Fi 6, BLE 5.3 and 802.15.4 (Thread/Zigbee) plus a low-power core; a cheap all-in-one choice for Matter devices and border routers.
mcus.core: RISC-V 32-bit (RV32IMAC) HP core + 20 MHz LP RISC-V core

mcus.name: ESP32-C61
mcus.description: Cost-optimised 160 MHz RISC-V Wi-Fi 6 + BLE SoC that adds PSRAM support; a Wi-Fi 6 upgrade path from the ESP32-C3 for memory-hungrier apps.

mcus.name: ESP32-H2
mcus.description: 96 MHz RISC-V SoC with BLE 5.3 and 802.15.4 (Thread/Zigbee) but no Wi-Fi; low-power choice for battery Matter-over-Thread and Zigbee end devices.

mcus.name: ESP32-P4
mcus.description: 400 MHz dual-core RISC-V application MCU (no radio) with up to 32 MB in-package PSRAM, MIPI-DSI/CSI, H.264/JPEG, USB 2.0 High-Speed and Ethernet for HMI and camera products.
mcus.core: RISC-V 32-bit dual-core HP (RV32IMAFC + AI/SIMD extensions) + 40 MHz LP RISC-V core

mcus.name: ESP8266EX
mcus.description: The original ultra-cheap Wi-Fi MCU; still fine for simple Arduino Wi-Fi projects via ESP-12F modules, but legacy (NRND) with few hardware peripherals.

mcus.name: GD32F303
mcus.description: 120 MHz Cortex-M4F STM32F103/F303-style workhorse with up to 1 MB flash, USB FS device, CAN, SDIO and 5 UARTs; cheap and widely stocked.

mcus.name: GD32VF103
mcus.description: Early mainstream RISC-V MCU (Longan Nano): 108 MHz, 128 KB flash, USB FS OTG with ROM DFU bootloader, 2x CAN and 5 UARTs in an STM32F103-like layout.

mcus.name: GD32E230
mcus.description: Low-cost 72 MHz Cortex-M23 with up to 64 KB flash, 2 USART/I2C/SPI and 1.8-3.6 V supply; an inexpensive STM32F030/G030-class part from about $0.40.

mcus.name: HPM5361
mcus.description: 480 MHz RISC-V MCU with 1 MB in-package flash, 4x CAN-FD, high-speed USB with built-in PHY and motor-control timers in QFN-48/LQFP; a cheap, fast pick for CAN-FD + USB designs.

mcus.name: HPM6750
mcus.description: Dual 816 MHz RISC-V MCU with 2 MB SRAM, 4x CAN-FD, two High-Speed USB OTG with PHYs, two gigabit Ethernet MACs, two SD/eMMC hosts, SDRAM, LCD and camera; MPU-class I/O without Linux.

mcus.name: HPM6280
mcus.description: Dual 600 MHz RISC-V MCU with 800 KB SRAM, 4x CAN-FD, High-Speed USB with PHY, 100 ps high-resolution PWM and 16-bit ADCs; aimed at digital power and motor control.

mcus.name: PSoC 62 (CY8C62xx)
mcus.description: Dual-core 150 MHz Cortex-M4F + Cortex-M0+ with up to 2 MB flash / 1 MB SRAM, CapSense touch, USB FS, SD host, QSPI XIP and crypto; a low-power, touch-capable MCU for IoT. It has no radio.

mcus.name: PSoC 4100S / 4100S Plus
mcus.description: 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ with best-in-class CapSense touch, opamps and a 12-bit SAR ADC, running from 1.71-5.5 V. The 4100S Plus adds 128 KB flash, 5 serial blocks and classic CAN.

mcus.name: XMC1100
mcus.description: Cheap 32 MHz Cortex-M0 in a hand-solderable TSSOP-38 that runs from 1.8-5.5 V, with a 12-bit ADC, RTC and two flexible USIC serial channels. A good 8-bit replacement.

mcus.name: XMC4700
mcus.description: 144 MHz Cortex-M4F industrial MCU with 2 MB flash, 352 KB SRAM, Ethernet, USB OTG, SD/MMC, six classic CAN nodes and rich motor-control timers. Good for gateways, PLC-style I/O and drives.

mcus.name: ATmega328P
mcus.description: The Arduino Uno chip: a breadboard-friendly 8-bit AVR in DIP-28 that runs straight from 5 V, with a huge library ecosystem and dead-simple hardware.

mcus.name: ATmega32U4
mcus.description: 8-bit AVR with native full-speed USB device (Arduino Leonardo / Pro Micro): great for USB keyboards, MIDI and HID gadgets at 5 V.

mcus.name: ATmega2560
mcus.description: The Arduino Mega chip: 86 I/O, 4 hardware serial ports and 256 KB flash in a 5 V 8-bit AVR, ideal for pin-hungry 3D printers and controllers.

mcus.name: ATmega4809
mcus.description: Modern 5 V megaAVR (Arduino Nano Every / Uno WiFi Rev2) with 4 USARTs, 48 KB flash, an RTC and simple 1-wire UPDI programming.

mcus.name: ATtiny85
mcus.description: Classic 8-pin DIP/SOIC AVR (Digispark, Adafruit Trinket): tiny 5 V jobs like LED drivers, sensors and simple controllers with Arduino support.

mcus.name: ATtiny412
mcus.description: Tiny, cheap 8-pin SOIC AVR with a real USART, I2C, SPI, DAC and event system; runs at 5 V and programs over a single UPDI wire.

mcus.name: ATtiny1616
mcus.description: 20-pin 5 V tinyAVR with 16 KB flash, two ADCs, a DAC and 12-channel hardware capacitive touch (PTC); cheap and UPDI-programmable.

mcus.name: ATtiny3224
mcus.description: 14-pin 5 V tinyAVR with 32 KB flash, two USARTs and a 12-bit differential ADC with programmable gain - great for small sensor front-ends.

mcus.name: AVR128DA
mcus.description: Biggest modern 5 V AVR: 128 KB flash, 16 KB RAM, up to 6 USARTs, 12-bit ADC, DAC and hardware touch, with DIP-28 to TQFP-64 options.

mcus.name: AVR128DB
mcus.description: 5 V AVR with multi-voltage I/O (talk to 1.8/3.3 V parts on one port), built-in op-amps and a crystal oscillator - good for mixed-signal and level-shifting jobs.

mcus.name: AVR64DD
mcus.description: Low-cost 5 V AVR from 14 to 32 pins with multi-voltage I/O, 12-bit ADC and DAC; a modern, cheap replacement for ATmega328-class designs.

mcus.name: AVR64EA
mcus.description: 5 V AVR focused on precision analog: 12-bit differential ADC with programmable gain, 10-bit DAC and very low 0.08 uA power-down current.

mcus.name: ATSAMD21
mcus.description: The Arduino Zero / Adafruit M0 chip: a cheap 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ with native USB, six flexible SERCOM serial ports and excellent CircuitPython support.

mcus.name: ATSAMD51
mcus.description: 120 MHz Cortex-M4F with FPU, 1 MB flash, 256 KB RAM, native USB, QSPI and SD host: the Adafruit M4 chip, great for CircuitPython, audio and displays.

mcus.name: ATSAME51
mcus.description: SAMD51 plus two CAN-FD controllers: a 120 MHz Cortex-M4F with USB, QSPI and SD host for CAN-connected robots, vehicles and industrial nodes.

mcus.name: ATSAME54
mcus.description: 120 MHz Cortex-M4F with 10/100 Ethernet MAC, two CAN-FD, USB, QSPI and two SD hosts - a single-chip gateway for Ethernet + CAN industrial designs.

mcus.name: ATSAME70
mcus.description: 300 MHz Cortex-M7 with double-precision FPU, 2 MB flash, High-Speed USB with on-chip PHY, Ethernet, two CAN-FD and a camera interface.

mcus.name: ATSAMC21
mcus.description: 5 V-capable 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ with two CAN-FD controllers, a 16-bit sigma-delta ADC and touch - built for robust 5 V automotive and industrial nodes.

mcus.name: ATSAML21
mcus.description: Ultra-low-power 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ (~40 uA/MHz, sub-uA backup) with USB, AES, 12-bit DAC and op-amps for battery-powered sensors.

mcus.name: PIC16F18446
mcus.description: Low-cost 5 V 8-bit PIC in DIP/SOIC/SSOP-20 with a 12-bit computing ADC, CLCs and core-independent peripherals for simple analog and control tasks.

mcus.name: PIC18F-Q84
mcus.description: 5 V 8-bit PIC with a built-in CAN FD controller, 5 UARTs, DMA and a 12-bit computing ADC; offered in hobbyist-friendly DIP-28/DIP-40.

mcus.name: dsPIC33CK256MP50x
mcus.description: 100 MIPS 16-bit DSC with CAN FD, 250 ps high-resolution PWM, three fast 12-bit ADCs and op-amps: aimed at motor control and digital power.

mcus.name: PIC32MZ EF
mcus.description: 200 MHz MIPS M-class MCU with double-precision FPU, 2 MB flash, 512 KB RAM, High-Speed USB with on-chip PHY, Ethernet MAC and two CAN 2.0B.

mcus.name: PIC32MK MCM
mcus.description: 120 MHz MIPS MCU with FPU and four CAN FD controllers, two USB, 7 fast ADCs, op-amps and motor-control PWM: a dense CAN FD motor/industrial chip.

mcus.name: PIC32CX-BZ2
mcus.description: Low-cost Cortex-M4F wireless SoC with Bluetooth LE 5.2 and Zigbee 3.0/Thread, 1 MB flash and hardware crypto; also sold as certified WBZ451 modules.

mcus.name: nRF52810
mcus.description: Entry-level Bluetooth LE SoC (Cortex-M4, 192 KB flash) for simple beacons, tags and sensors where cost matters more than RAM or peripherals.

mcus.name: nRF52832
mcus.description: The classic Bluetooth LE SoC: Cortex-M4F, 512 KB flash, NFC tag and a huge choice of cheap modules and community support.

mcus.name: nRF52833
mcus.description: Mid-range nRF52 with USB, 512 KB flash, +8 dBm radio, Bluetooth Long Range/direction finding and Thread/Zigbee; the chip in the BBC micro:bit v2.

mcus.name: nRF52840
mcus.description: The go-to Bluetooth LE + Thread/Zigbee/Matter SoC with native USB, QSPI, 1 MB flash and 256 KB RAM; huge board ecosystem (Feather, XIAO, nice!nano).

mcus.name: nRF5340
mcus.description: Dual Cortex-M33 (128 MHz app + 64 MHz network core) for LE Audio, Matter and Thread, with USB, QSPI, 1 MB + 256 KB flash and TrustZone security.

mcus.name: nRF54L15
mcus.description: Nordic's newest mainstream BLE/Thread/Matter SoC: 128 MHz Cortex-M33 plus RISC-V coprocessor, 1.5 MB RRAM, Bluetooth 6.0 Channel Sounding, in an easy QFN48. Cheaper than the nRF52840.

mcus.name: nRF9151
mcus.description: Pre-certified LTE-M/NB-IoT + GNSS (and DECT NR+) system-in-package with a user-programmable Cortex-M33, for battery-powered cellular IoT trackers and sensors.

mcus.name: LPC55S69
mcus.description: Dual 150 MHz Cortex-M33 with TrustZone, crypto/PUF, high-speed USB with on-chip PHY plus full-speed USB and an SD/SDIO host; a secure, well-documented general-purpose MCU.

mcus.name: LPC845
mcus.description: Low-cost 30 MHz Cortex-M0+ with a switch matrix that routes any function to any pin, 5 USARTs, 4 I2C, two DACs and capacitive touch, in hand-solderable LQFP.

mcus.name: LPC1768
mcus.description: Classic 100 MHz Cortex-M3 (the original mbed) with Ethernet MAC, USB host/device/OTG, two classic CAN channels and 512 KB flash in an LQFP-100.

mcus.name: MCXA153
mcus.description: Cheap 96 MHz Cortex-M33 with crystal-less full-speed USB device, 16-bit ADC and motor-control PWM; NXP's modern entry-level MCU with USB/UART ROM bootloader.

mcus.name: MCXN947
mcus.description: Dual 150 MHz Cortex-M33 with NPU, 2 MB flash, 2x CAN-FD, high-speed USB with PHY, Ethernet, SDHC and rich analog; a feature-packed modern NXP MCU.

mcus.name: i.MX RT1011
mcus.description: The cheapest 500 MHz Cortex-M7 in a hand-solderable LQFP-80, with high-speed USB OTG (on-chip PHY) and QSPI XIP; great for fast audio/USB gadgets.

mcus.name: i.MX RT1062
mcus.description: 600 MHz Cortex-M7 with 1 MB SRAM, 2x high-speed USB, 2x Ethernet, 2x SD, LCD and camera interfaces; the Teensy 4.x chip with a huge Arduino ecosystem.

mcus.name: i.MX RT1176
mcus.description: 1 GHz Cortex-M7 plus 400 MHz Cortex-M4 with 2 MB SRAM, 3x CAN-FD, 2x HS USB, gigabit Ethernet, MIPI-DSI/CSI and 2D GPU; an MPU-class MCU for HMI and gateways.

mcus.name: S32K144
mcus.description: AEC-Q100 automotive Cortex-M4F running from 2.7-5.5 V with 3 FlexCAN (1 CAN-FD), 512 KB flash and LIN-capable UARTs; cheap and robust for 5 V/12 V vehicle electronics.

mcus.name: S32K344
mcus.description: ASIL-D lockstep 160 MHz Cortex-M7 with 6 CAN-FD controllers, 16 LPUARTs, 4 MB flash and 100 Mbit Ethernet, running from 3.3 or 5 V; a top pick for multi-CAN-FD automotive tools.

mcus.name: MKL25Z128
mcus.description: 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ with USB OTG full-speed, 16-bit ADC, DAC and 16 capacitive-touch channels; the chip on the classic FRDM-KL25Z board.

mcus.name: STC8H8K64U
mcus.description: Cheap 1T 8051 with native USB and a USB-HID bootloader (flash with just a cable), 64 KB flash, 4 UARTs, 12-bit ADC and a 1.9-5.5 V supply.

mcus.name: M031
mcus.description: Long-lived Nuvoton Cortex-M0 family (48 MHz, 16-128 KB flash) with 1.8-3.6 V supply, 5 V tolerant I/O and a 2 MSPS 12-bit ADC.

mcus.name: M487
mcus.description: 192 MHz Cortex-M4F with USB 2.0 High-Speed OTG (on-chip PHY) plus FS OTG, Ethernet MAC, 2x CAN, 2x SD host and crypto engines.

mcus.name: K210
mcus.description: Dual-core 64-bit RISC-V AI SoC (400 MHz, 8 MB SRAM) with a CNN accelerator (KPU), audio processor and camera port; the chip in Sipeed Maix boards.

mcus.name: PY32F002A
mcus.description: One of the cheapest 32-bit MCUs (~$0.10 in volume): 24 MHz Cortex-M0+, 20 KB flash, runs from 1.7-5.5 V, SOP-8 to TSSOP-20, UART-flashable.

mcus.name: PY32F003
mcus.description: Ultra-cheap 32 MHz Cortex-M0+ with up to 64 KB flash / 8 KB RAM, 2 USARTs, DMA and RTC, running from 1.7-5.5 V for about $0.15 in volume.

mcus.name: PY32F030
mcus.description: Low-cost 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ with 64 KB flash, 2 SPI, 2 USART, up to 30 GPIO and a 1.7-5.5 V supply; a cheap 5 V-capable STM32F030-class part.

mcus.name: RP2040
mcus.description: Dual-core Cortex-M0+ with 8 PIO state machines; cheap, hugely popular, drag-and-drop UF2 flashing over USB.

mcus.name: RP2350
mcus.description: RP2040 successor with dual Cortex-M33 (or Hazard3 RISC-V) cores at 150 MHz, 520 KB SRAM, 12 PIO state machines and secure boot; still cheap and UF2-flashable.
mcus.core: Arm Cortex-M33 (or Hazard3 RISC-V, selectable at boot)

mcus.name: RA0E1
mcus.description: Very cheap (~$0.50) 32 MHz Cortex-M23 that runs straight from 1.6-5.5 V with ~0.2 uA standby; good for small 5 V sensor, glue-logic and battery jobs in 16- to 32-pin packages.

mcus.name: RA2E1
mcus.description: Low-power 48 MHz Cortex-M23 that runs from 1.6-5.5 V, with up to 30 capacitive-touch channels and AES; a cheap 5 V-capable general-purpose MCU in packages from 25 to 64 pins.

mcus.name: RA4M1
mcus.description: The Arduino Uno R4 chip: a 48 MHz Cortex-M4F that runs from 1.6-5.5 V with USB FS (host/device), one classic CAN, segment LCD, 14-bit ADC, DAC and capacitive touch.

mcus.name: RA4E2
mcus.description: 100 MHz Cortex-M33 with one CAN-FD channel, USB FS device, I3C and I2S in small 32- to 64-pin packages; one of the cheapest ways to get CAN-FD on a modern Arm core.

mcus.name: RA6M5
mcus.description: 200 MHz Cortex-M33 with 2 MB flash, 512 KB RAM, Ethernet, USB HS (internal PHY) + USB FS, two CAN-FD, SDHI, QSPI/OSPI and a strong crypto engine; a connected-gateway workhorse.

mcus.name: RA8M1
mcus.description: Cortex-M85 with Helium at up to 480 MHz, 2 MB flash, 1 MB SRAM, Ethernet, USB HS + FS, two CAN-FD, two SDHI, OSPI and a camera input; Renesas' high-end MCU for DSP/ML and gateways.

mcus.name: EFR32MG24
mcus.description: Matter/Thread/Zigbee + Bluetooth LE SoC with a 78 MHz Cortex-M33, 1.5 MB flash, 256 KB RAM, AI/ML accelerator and Secure Vault; used in XIAO MG24 and Arduino Nano Matter.

mcus.name: EFR32BG22
mcus.description: Low-cost, ultra-low-power Bluetooth LE SoC (76.8 MHz Cortex-M33, 512 KB flash) with direction finding (AoA/AoD), ideal for coin-cell sensors, tags and beacons.

mcus.name: EFR32MG21
mcus.description: High-performance 2.4 GHz Zigbee/Thread/BLE SoC with an 80 MHz Cortex-M33 and +20 dBm PA in a small QFN32. The chip behind many Zigbee/Thread USB coordinators.

mcus.name: EFM8BB1
mcus.description: Tiny, cheap 25 MHz 8051 with 8 KB flash, 12-bit ADC and comparators in SOIC16/QSOP24/QFN20. Good for simple control jobs if you are comfortable with 8051 C.

mcus.name: STM32C011
mcus.description: ST's cheapest 32-bit MCU: 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ with 32 KB flash in SO-8 or TSSOP-20, a modern drop-in for 8-bit parts.

mcus.name: STM32C031
mcus.description: Low-cost 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ with 32 KB flash and 12 KB RAM in TSSOP-20 to LQFP-48; a cheap general-purpose 32-bit replacement for 8-bit MCUs.

mcus.name: STM32C071
mcus.description: Low-cost 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ with 128 KB flash and crystal-less USB FS device/host; a cheap way to add native USB to a small design.

mcus.name: STM32C092
mcus.description: Cheapest STM32 with CAN-FD: 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ with 256 KB flash, one FDCAN and 4 USARTs, even in TSSOP-20.

mcus.name: STM32F030
mcus.description: Long-running 48 MHz Cortex-M0 value line; dirt cheap and well documented, with up to 256 KB flash and 6 USARTs on the larger parts.

mcus.name: STM32F042
mcus.description: Small 48 MHz Cortex-M0 with crystal-less USB FS device, CAN and a USB DFU bootloader in TSSOP-20; a classic for USB-CAN adapters and tiny USB gadgets.

mcus.name: STM32F072
mcus.description: 48 MHz Cortex-M0 with 128 KB flash, crystal-less USB FS device, CAN, 2-channel DAC and 24 touch channels; widely used in USB keyboards and adapters.

mcus.name: STM32F103
mcus.description: The classic 72 MHz Cortex-M3 of the "Blue Pill": cheap, everywhere, huge community; has USB FS device and CAN but is dated versus G0/G4/F4.

mcus.name: STM32F303
mcus.description: 72 MHz Cortex-M4F with strong analog: 4 fast 12-bit ADCs, comparators, op-amps and DAC, plus USB FS device and CAN.

mcus.name: STM32F401
mcus.description: Entry-level 84 MHz Cortex-M4F with up to 512 KB flash and USB OTG FS; the chip on the cheap "Black Pill" boards.

mcus.name: STM32F411
mcus.description: 100 MHz Cortex-M4F with 512 KB flash, 128 KB RAM, USB OTG FS and five SPI/I2S; the popular "Black Pill" upgrade with broad Arduino/MicroPython support.

mcus.name: STM32F405
mcus.description: Classic 168 MHz Cortex-M4F with 1 MB flash, 192 KB RAM, 2x CAN, USB OTG FS + HS and SDIO; powers the pyboard, Adafruit Feather STM32F405 and many flight controllers.

mcus.name: STM32F407
mcus.description: The STM32F405 plus 10/100 Ethernet MAC and camera interface: 168 MHz Cortex-M4F, 1 MB flash, 2x CAN, USB OTG FS + HS; very common on cheap dev boards.

mcus.name: STM32F446
mcus.description: 180 MHz Cortex-M4F with 512 KB flash, 2x CAN, USB OTG FS + HS, Quad-SPI, SAI audio and camera interface; a fast all-rounder found on NUCLEO-F446RE.

mcus.name: STM32F722
mcus.description: Budget 216 MHz Cortex-M7 with 512 KB flash, 256 KB RAM, USB OTG FS + HS, 2x SDMMC and Quad-SPI; popular in flight controllers.

mcus.name: STM32F767
mcus.description: 216 MHz Cortex-M7 with double-precision FPU, 2 MB flash, 512 KB RAM, Ethernet, 3x CAN, USB HS/FS, LCD-TFT, camera and JPEG codec.

mcus.name: STM32G030
mcus.description: Bare-bones 64 MHz Cortex-M0+ value line with up to 64 KB flash; very cheap and popular as a small helper MCU.

mcus.name: STM32G031
mcus.description: Cheap 64 MHz Cortex-M0+ with up to 64 KB flash, LPUART, low-power timers and RTC, from SO-8 to LQFP-48.

mcus.name: STM32G071
mcus.description: 64 MHz Cortex-M0+ with 128 KB flash, two USB Type-C Power Delivery (UCPD) controllers, 2-channel DAC and 5 UARTs; ideal for USB-C PD sinks/sources.

mcus.name: STM32G0B1
mcus.description: Feature-packed 64 MHz Cortex-M0+: up to 512 KB flash, 144 KB RAM, 2x CAN-FD, crystal-less USB device/host, USB-C PD and 8 UARTs; great value for CAN/USB gadgets.

mcus.name: STM32G431
mcus.description: 170 MHz Cortex-M4F mixed-signal MCU with CAN-FD, USB FS, UCPD, CORDIC/FMAC math accelerators and fast analog; a favourite for motor control and power conversion.

mcus.name: STM32G474
mcus.description: 170 MHz Cortex-M4F with a 184 ps high-resolution timer (HRTIM), 5 ADCs, 7 DACs, 3x CAN-FD, Quad-SPI and USB FS; the go-to for digital power and advanced motor control.

mcus.name: STM32G491
mcus.description: Mid-range 170 MHz Cortex-M4F with 512 KB flash, 2x CAN-FD, Quad-SPI, 3 ADCs and USB FS; more memory than the G431 without the G474 price.

mcus.name: STM32H503
mcus.description: Low-cost 250 MHz Cortex-M33 with 128 KB flash, CAN-FD, USB FS, I3C and a 2-channel DAC; lots of speed for small control tasks.

mcus.name: STM32H563
mcus.description: Fast 250 MHz Cortex-M33 with TrustZone, 2 MB flash, 640 KB RAM, Ethernet, 2x CAN-FD, USB-C PD and Octo-SPI; a modern replacement for F4/F7 designs.

mcus.name: STM32H723
mcus.description: Cheapest 550 MHz Cortex-M7: 1 MB flash, 564 KB RAM, 3x CAN-FD, Ethernet, 2x Octo-SPI and LCD-TFT in hand-solderable LQFP packages.

mcus.name: STM32H743
mcus.description: Classic 480 MHz Cortex-M7 workhorse with 2 MB flash, 1 MB RAM, Ethernet, 2x CAN-FD, USB HS/FS, LCD-TFT and camera interface; widely used in flight controllers.

mcus.name: STM32H747
mcus.description: Dual-core 480 MHz Cortex-M7 + 240 MHz Cortex-M4 with 2 MB flash, 1 MB RAM, MIPI-DSI display, Ethernet and USB HS; the chip in Arduino Portenta H7 and GIGA R1.

mcus.name: STM32L031
mcus.description: Ultra-low-power 32 MHz Cortex-M0+ with 32 KB flash, LPUART and EEPROM; sips sub-microamp currents in coin-cell sensor nodes.

mcus.name: STM32L432
mcus.description: Ultra-low-power 80 MHz Cortex-M4F in a tiny 32-pin package with CAN, crystal-less USB, Quad-SPI and DAC; the NUCLEO-L432KC chip.

mcus.name: STM32L476
mcus.description: Ultra-low-power 80 MHz Cortex-M4F with 1 MB flash, USB OTG FS, segment LCD driver, SDMMC, Quad-SPI and CAN; a flexible low-power workhorse.

mcus.name: STM32U031
mcus.description: Ultra-low-power 56 MHz Cortex-M0+ (160 nA standby with RTC) with 64 KB flash, 6 UARTs and capacitive touch; for battery-powered sensors.

mcus.name: STM32U575
mcus.description: Ultra-low-power 160 MHz Cortex-M33 with TrustZone, 2 MB flash and 786 KB RAM, CAN-FD, USB OTG with Type-C PD, 2x Octo-SPI and a 14-bit ADC.

mcus.name: STM32U585
mcus.description: STM32U575 plus hardware AES/SAES, PKA and on-the-fly external memory decryption; the secure ultra-low-power Cortex-M33 used in ST IoT reference designs.

mcus.name: STM32WB55
mcus.description: Bluetooth LE + 802.15.4 (Thread/Zigbee/Matter) dual-core MCU: 64 MHz Cortex-M4 for the app, Cortex-M0+ for the radio, 1 MB flash, USB FS and a mature ST stack.

mcus.name: STM32WBA55
mcus.description: Single-core 100 MHz Cortex-M33 wireless MCU for Bluetooth LE, Thread, Zigbee and Matter with TrustZone, SESIP3 security and very low radio current.

mcus.name: STM32WL55
mcus.description: LoRa / sub-GHz SoC with dual Cortex-M4 + M0+ cores, 256 KB flash and a 150-960 MHz radio (LoRa, (G)FSK, BPSK) with up to +22 dBm output.

mcus.name: STM32WLE5
mcus.description: Single-core Cortex-M4 LoRa / sub-GHz SoC (150-960 MHz, up to +22 dBm); the chip inside popular modules like Seeed LoRa-E5 and RAK3172.

mcus.name: STM32N657
mcus.description: Edge-AI MCU: 800 MHz Cortex-M55 with Helium plus a 600 GOPS Neural-ART NPU, 4.2 MB SRAM, MIPI CSI-2 camera + ISP, H.264 encoder, Gigabit Ethernet and 2x USB HS.

mcus.name: MSPM0C1104
mcus.description: Tiny 24 MHz Cortex-M0+ for sub-$0.50 jobs: 16 KB flash, 12-bit ADC and timers in packages down to SOT-23-8 and a 1.6 mm WCSP; great for replacing 8-bit MCUs.

mcus.name: MSPM0L1306
mcus.description: Low-power 32 MHz Cortex-M0+ with 64 KB flash, 1.68 Msps 12-bit ADC and two zero-drift op-amps; a cheap analog sensor front-end with a ROM UART/I2C bootloader.

mcus.name: MSPM0G3507
mcus.description: 80 MHz Cortex-M0+ with CAN-FD, two 4 Msps 12-bit ADCs, DAC, comparators and op-amps for about $1-3; a cheap pick for motor control and CAN-FD nodes.

mcus.name: MSP430FR2433
mcus.description: Ultra-low-power 16-bit MSP430 with 15.5 KB FRAM (fast, high-endurance non-volatile memory) and ~1 µA sleep with RTC; good for coin-cell sensors and data logging.

mcus.name: MSP430G2553
mcus.description: Classic low-power 16-bit MCU in a breadboard-friendly DIP-20; the chip from the MSP-EXP430G2 LaunchPad, ideal for learning and very simple battery gadgets.

mcus.name: CC2340R5
mcus.description: Low-cost 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ Bluetooth LE 5.4 SoC (also Zigbee and Thread) with 512 KB flash, under 1 µA standby and roughly $1-2 pricing.

mcus.name: CC2652R
mcus.description: 48 MHz Cortex-M4F multiprotocol 2.4 GHz SoC for Zigbee, Thread and BLE 5.2 with a low-power sensor controller; a well-proven Zigbee/Thread workhorse.

mcus.name: CC1352P
mcus.description: Dual-band Sub-1 GHz + 2.4 GHz Cortex-M4F SoC with an integrated +20 dBm PA: long-range sub-GHz links plus Zigbee, Thread and BLE 5.2 on one chip.

mcus.name: CC3235S
mcus.description: Dual-band (2.4 + 5 GHz) Wi-Fi 4 SoC with an 80 MHz Cortex-M4 app core and an offloaded TCP/IP + TLS network processor; pick it when you need 5 GHz Wi-Fi.

mcus.name: TM4C123GH6PM
mcus.description: 80 MHz Cortex-M4F with lots of I/O: 8 UARTs, 4 I2C, 4 SPI, 2 CAN, USB OTG and 16 motor-control PWMs; the chip on the classic Tiva C LaunchPad.

mcus.name: CH32V003
mcus.description: The famous 10-cent RISC-V MCU: 48 MHz, 16 KB flash, runs straight from 5 V, down to SOP-8; ideal for tiny glue logic and replacing 8-bit parts.

mcus.name: CH32V006
mcus.description: Bigger brother of the CH32V003: 62 KB flash, 8 KB RAM, 12-bit ADC, two UARTs and touch keys, still 5 V tolerant supply and under $0.35.

mcus.name: CH32V203
mcus.description: Cheap 144 MHz RISC-V STM32F103 alternative with two USB controllers (device + host/OTG), CAN and 4 UARTs from about $0.65.

mcus.name: CH32V305
mcus.description: Cheapest way to get USB 2.0 High-Speed with a built-in PHY, plus 2x CAN, SDIO and an FPU, in packages down to TSSOP-20.

mcus.name: CH32V307
mcus.description: Feature-packed 144 MHz RISC-V with FPU: USB HS with PHY + USB FS OTG, Ethernet with built-in 10M PHY, 2x CAN, SDIO, camera port and 8 UARTs for about $3.

mcus.name: CH32X035
mcus.description: Low-cost RISC-V with USB FS host/device plus a built-in USB PD / Type-C controller and PHY, runs from 2-5.5 V; great for USB-C gadgets and PD sinks.

mcus.name: CH32L103
mcus.description: Probably the cheapest CAN-FD MCU (~$0.80): 96 MHz low-power RISC-V with USB FS host/device, USB PD/Type-C, 4 UARTs and sub-1 uA standby.

mcus.name: CH552
mcus.description: Classic ~$0.55 8051 with native USB device and a factory USB bootloader; runs from 5 V with an internal 3.3 V regulator, down to MSOP-10.

mcus.name: CH582
mcus.description: Cheap BLE 5 RISC-V SoC with two USB FS host/device controllers, 448 KB flash, AES and sub-1 uA sleep for about $1.10.

mcus.name: CH592
mcus.description: Ultra-cheap BLE 5.4 RISC-V SoC (~$0.70) with USB FS host/device, segment-LCD driver, AES and 1.7 V operation; good for coin-cell BLE gadgets.

mcus.name: BL602/BL604
mcus.description: Very cheap 192 MHz RISC-V Wi-Fi 4 + BLE 5.0 SoC with an FPU; an ESP8266-class alternative (e.g. Ai-WB2 modules) if you can live with a smaller ecosystem.

mcus.name: BL616/BL618
mcus.description: 320 MHz RISC-V SoC with Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3 dual-mode and 802.15.4, plus USB 2.0 High-Speed, Ethernet, SD host, camera and display interfaces at a very low price.

mcus.name: RTL8720DN
mcus.description: Dual-band (2.4 + 5 GHz) Wi-Fi 4 + BLE 5.0 SoC with a 200 MHz Cortex-M33-class core; the cheap BW16 module is the easiest way to get 5 GHz Wi-Fi in Arduino.
mcus.core: Real-M300 (Arm Cortex-M33 compatible, 200 MHz) + Real-M200 (Cortex-M23 compatible) low-power core
